sites.name: Midwest Steel & Iron Works Company Complex
overview: The Midwest Steel & Iron Works Company complex at 25 Larimer Street was the headquarters of one of Denver's oldest and largest structural and ornamental metal fabricators. The four-building industrial complex reflects the city's growth as a regional manufacturing and engineering center.
timeline: 1906 — Initial construction began at the Larimer Street complex.
1923 — The Larimer Street complex became Midwest Steel & Iron Works Company's headquarters.
1930 — Denver architect Roland L. Linder designed an Art Deco office addition, an unusual application of the style to an industrial site.

1983 — The Larimer Street complex ended its long period as the company's headquarters; the site was also determined eligible for the National Register of Historic Places for its industrial and architectural significance.
moreHistory: Historic American Engineering Record documentation identifies Midwest Steel & Iron Works as a major regional fabricator of structural and ornamental metal components used in buildings and engineering works across Colorado, Wyoming, and New Mexico. The surviving Larimer Street complex includes industrial, office, repair, and storage functions that illustrate Denver's twentieth-century metal-fabrication industry.
